title: Treasury liquidity-support buyback operation (7-10Y nominal, $4B cap, 1:40pm ET)
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Buyback Operations (August 2026 refunding, masthead 'For Publication August 5, 2026'), PDF text layer decompressed direct 2026-09-08 (plain curl, HTTP 200, 125,547 bytes, md5 79b65955e74a59f6bebff3adf8ba7b35) — the row reads verbatim announce 9/16/2026, operation 9/17/2026 1:40 pm - 2:00 pm, settle 9/18/2026, Liquidity Support, Nominal Coupons 7Y to 10Y, maturity range 09/18/2033 - 09/17/2036, min $0, max $4 billion. Stays estimate on the two counts the sibling treasury-buyback-2y3y-2026-10-06 entry already documented: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and the confirming primary is the 09-16 operation announcement rather than this document, checked 2026-09-08
notes: DISCOVERED during the treasury-buyback-increase-2026-09-09 D-1 pulse-check adjacency sweep (2026-09-08), reading the same schedule PDF that event re-fetches every pulse. WHY THIS ONE IS WORTH TRACKING RATHER THAN JUST NOTED: it is the parity benchmark for the whole sb0607 story. Read down the August-refunding schedule's nominal-coupon rows and every OTHER sector already ran a $4B cap before sb0607 existed — 1Mo-2Y $4B (08/06), 3Y-5Y $4B (08/21), 5Y-7Y $4B (08/26), this 7Y-10Y $4B (09/17), 2Y-3Y $4B (10/06) — while ONLY 10Y-20Y and 20Y-30Y sat at $2B. So the 09-09 increase does not create a new size tier; it lifts the two long-end buckets to the size the rest of the nominal curve already had. That reframes the event from 'extraordinary intervention' toward 'removing the long end's discount', and this operation is the standing control that makes the comparison legible. It also lands the DAY AFTER the 09-16 FOMC and inside the same corridor, so its own tape read will be confounded. Two cautions for whoever researches it. First, the $4B here is the STANDING cap for this bucket, NOT the figure sb0607 doubled — do not read it as evidence the increase took effect. Second, the cap does not bind in this bucket: measured 2026-09-08 off fiscaldata's buybacks_operations, 7Y-10Y has filled its cap 0 times in 9 operations, against 10Y-20Y at 25/25 and 20Y-30Y at 24/26. Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
